message.content: The Milwaukee Bucks won the 2021 NBA Finals. They defeated the Phoenix Suns in six games to claim their first championship since 1971 [4]. This victory ended a 50-year championship drought for the Bucks [1]. Giannis Antetokounmpo was named Finals MVP [1].

passages.heading: 2021 NBA Finals
passages.text: Milwaukee and Phoenix were two of five teams in the league with an active championship drought of 50 years or more.<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup><sup>[5]</sup> Prior to 2021, the Bucks won their only title in 1971, while the Suns have yet to win a title since joining the league in 1968. They were both making their third Finals appearance. Phoenix and Milwaukee each began play as expansion teams in 1968. Both teams were involved in a coin toss for the rights to the first overall pick in the 1969 NBA draft, which the Bucks won and used to select Lew Alcindor, later known as Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, from UCLA. He led the Bucks to their first championship in 1971.<sup>[6]</sup> The 2021 Finals was the first since 1971 to not include any players who had previously won an NBA championship, and the first since 2015 that no players on the winning team had prior NBA Finals experience. The Suns' Jae Crowder was the only player in the series who previously played in the Finals (having made the Finals in 2020 with the Miami Heat), making it just the second time since the first Finals that fewer than two players had previously appeared in the championship series; no players had previously played in the Finals in the 1977 series.<sup>[7]</sup>

passages.heading: **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**

The Celtics have the most NBA titles with 18. Here’s a list of teams that have won at least three NBA championships:

- Boston Celtics (18 titles)
- Los Angeles Lakers (17)
- Golden State Warriors (7)
- Chicago Bulls (6)
- San Antonio Spurs (5)
- Philadelphia 76ers (3)
- Detroit Pistons (3)
- Miami Heat (3)

passages.heading: **Which players have won the most NBA championships?**
passages.text:

Bill Russell holds the record for most NBA rings with 11. Here is a list of NBA players with six titles or more:

- Sam Jones (10)
- K. C. Jones (8)

- Michael Jordan (6)
- Scottie Pippen (6)

passages.heading: **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**

Ten NBA franchises have never won an NBA Finals:

- Brooklyn Nets
- Charlotte Hornets
- Indiana Pacers
- Los Angeles Clippers
- Memphis Grizzlies
- Minnesota Timberwolves
- New Orleans Pelicans
- Orlando Magic
- Phoenix Suns
- Utah Jazz

sources.title: Your memories from the Milwaukee Bucks winning the 2021 NBA title

passages.text:
The five-year anniversary of the Milwaukee Bucks winning the 2021 NBA championship has come and gone, and it's a little bittersweet in the aftermath of Milwaukee trading franchise cornerstone Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat. But the memories will endure forever for Milwaukee fans.

Bucks reporter Jim Owczarski revisited many of those memories with new interviews from the players, coaches and others involved. They included chapters on P.J. Tucker, Mike Budenholzer, Game 6, the Jrue Holiday steal in Game 5, the workout that helped Giannis get back to game play.

We asked readers what they remembered about July 20, 2021, the day Milwaukee hoisted the trophy thanks to a Game 6 win over the Phoenix Suns in the NBA Finals. Here's what you told us:

It was amazing!" - Mac, Milwaukee

- "For my wife and I, game 1 vs. Miami at the Deer District was our first big outing post COVID. A sunny, daytime game with others!" – Jason, West Allis
- "Giannis' big game in the deciding game." – Kurt, River Falls
- "I was driving back to Arizona from Wisconsin and watching game 6 in Texas at a packed bar but only two tables watching the game. Ours and Suns fans! Fun!" – John Francois, Phoenix, Arizona
- "Being in the building for the last timeout when everyone knew the Bucks had the game won. Unreal." – Pat, Columbia, Missouri
- "Was overnight in Reno, Nevada, on a trip to Vegas with kids. Told them Bucks stories and finished with 'Bucks in 6.' Had to bet on Bucks in 6 of course. WINNER. Wouldn't cash the ticket unless I could keep it." – Mark Ellis, Lebanon, New Hampshire
- "Being there to witness Game 6 in person with my son, who was 20 years old at the time, and experiencing the championship events is a lasting memory." – Garry, Houston, Texas
- "Being there with my son - greatest night of our lives. Then heading to the Ambassador where we joined my wife and were up until 2 in the morning!" – Paul Krueger, Sheboygan
